claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'DELETE statement' followed by the indented sub-entry 'Indexed I-O module, IX-21'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'DELETE statement' then '  Indexed I-O module, IX-21'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use nested '- ' list items and keep them). Index is informative; the entry text and page references themselves match the PDF.

verdict.reasoning: Both sources are quoted accurately. The printed page B-53 (PDF p965) shows a two-column index whose sub-entries are indented under main entries. The markdown page-965.md keeps every entry on its own line, in order, with each sub-entry indented two spaces under its main entry (DELETE statement / '  Indexed I-O module, IX-21' / '  Relative I-O module, VIII-19', and so on), and the wrapped continuation 'COBOL, XVII-16' is indented further. Nothing is missing and no page reference changes, as the claim itself concedes. The hierarchy is in the source text as indentation. The only difference is how a Markdown renderer would lay out bare lines, and the page differs in style from pages 961-962, which use '- ' list markers. That is a formatting and rendering difference on an informative index page, with no change to content or meaning, so it is not a genuine content discrepancy.
